text:
The Golden Knights are 13-5-3 in their tenth season, with points in six straight (the last a shootout loss to Nashville on Friday) and a 98% chance at the playoffs by our numbers. They have a coin-flip shot at the division, 48%. Nothing about this start is a fluke: Vegas has taken 55% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, and its record is only a couple of points ahead of what that play deserves.

The top line is doing exactly what it should. Jack Eichel, Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev have outscored teams 10-4 together, and Brayden McNabb and Shea Theodore have been on for 20 goals for and 10 against as the top pair. Adin Hill has stopped 93% of shots over his last five starts, 5.4 goals better than expected.

The fun story is further down. Victor Olofsson has 10 points in eight games on a hot third line with Tomas Hertl, well above his chances (4.9 expected), so enjoy it while it lasts. Rookie Trevor Connelly has earned a look on Eichel's wing. Hertl's hit on Nashville's Mavrik Bourque is the one to watch: Markerzone reports Player Safety may step in.

The weak spots are the fourth line (Nic Dowd's group has 32% of the expected goals) and the second pair of Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon at 41%. For a team this good, that's where the playoff lineup will be decided.
headline: Vegas keeps banking points
